# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Madrasi_2014_tenofovir_qsp"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Madrasi_2014_tenofovir_qsp"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1038/psp.2014.46> (PMC4260001, open access)
* Supplement: the supplementary text (assumptions and Equations S1a-S2f),
  Supplementary Table S1 (parameter values), the authors' MATLAB code for the
  single- and multiple-dose simulations, their NONMEM 7.2 control stream for
  the population simulation, and Supplementary Figures S1-S4.

Madrasi 2014 builds an exploratory mechanistic model of how plasma tenofovir
(TFV), released from oral tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF), gets into
peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and is phosphorylated there to the
active anabolite tenofovir diphosphate (TFV-DP). Plasma tenofovir follows a
literature two-compartment model (Duwal 2012). Inside the PBMC the model
resolves the uptake and efflux mechanisms that empirical popPK models lump
into one rate constant: a saturable antiporter driven by the glutathione
gradient across the cell membrane, a saturable transporter efflux, a fast
first-order MRP4 leak back to plasma, optional passive diffusion of the
unionised fraction, and two Michaelis-Menten phosphorylation steps (adenylate
kinase 2, then nucleoside diphosphate kinase A).

Nothing in the model was estimated. The authors took every value from the
literature, then lowered the uptake Km 5000-fold and raised the leak about
2000-fold until TFV-DP formation saturated above a 300 mg dose, which is the
behaviour they set out to explain. The model was then taken to a 100-subject
population, with between-subject variability on the plasma PK only, and
compared with the oral arm of MTN-001.

The paper reports three model variants, all sharing this file's structure:

| Variant | Paper figures | `km_pbmc` (uM) | `keff_pbmc` (1/h) | `ps_pbmc` (L/h) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Diffusion + channel uptake | Figure 2, Figure S1 | 770 | 1.5e7 | 0.163 |
| Channel uptake only | Figure 3, Figure S2 | 770 | 1.5e7 | 0 |
| Saturable uptake (final; the packaged defaults) | Figures 4, 5, S3, S4; Table 1 | 0.154 | 3.4e10 | 0 |

# Population

The model was not fitted to data, so there is no estimation cohort. The
deterministic simulations are of a single typical adult receiving 75, 150,
300 or 600 mg TDF. The population simulation (Methods "Model validation") is
of 100 subjects taking 300 mg TDF once daily for 14 days with full adherence,
compared with steady-state plasma TFV and PBMC TFV-DP from the oral arm of
MTN-001 (Hendrix 2013): healthy, HIV-negative women taking daily oral TDF for
six weeks, sampled over 8 hours. The paper gives no demographics of its own,
and the model has no covariates.

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Madrasi_2014_tenofovir_qsp"))$population)
```

# Source trace

Every equation and every `ini()` value, with its location in the source. "Code"
means the authors' supplementary MATLAB or NONMEM listing.

| Item | Value in model | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Two-compartment plasma TFV PK with first-order absorption | `d/dt(depot)`, `d/dt(central)`, `d/dt(peripheral1)` | Figure 1; Supplement Eq. S2a, S2b, S2f; NONMEM `$DES` |
| Bioavailability on the absorbed TDF dose | `f(depot) = 0.32` | Table S1 `Fbio`; code `FB=0.32` |
| `lka` | log(1) 1/h | Table S1 `Ka`; code `KA=1` |
| `lcl` | log(29.28) L/h | Table S1 `Cl`; NONMEM `$THETA(1)` |
| `lvc` | log(244) L | Table S1 `Vc`; NONMEM `$THETA(2)` |
| `lvp` | log(464.54) L | Table S1 `Vp`; NONMEM `$THETA(3)` |
| `lq` | log(71.41) L/h | Table S1 `Q`; code `Q=71.41` |
| `fu` | 0.93 | Table S1 `fu`; code `FU=0.93` |
| `n_pbmc` | 0.9e6 cells/mL | Table S1 `N` |
| `v_blood` | 5 L | Table S1 `Vbl` |
| `v_pbmc_cell` | 0.28 pL | Table S1 `Vcell`; code `VC1` |
| Total PBMC volume `v_pbmc = n_pbmc x v_blood x v_pbmc_cell` | 1.26e-3 L | Eq. S1i denominator; code `VC2 = VC1 * N` with `N = 4.5e9` |
| Glutathione-driven saturable influx | `uptake` | Eq. S1h; code |
| Saturable efflux | `efflux` | Eq. S1i; code |
| `vmax_pbmc` | 1.77 g/(L h) | Table S1 `Vmax`; code `VMAX=1.77` |
| `km_pbmc` | 0.154 uM | Table S1 `Km` (assumed for model); code `KM=0.000044229` g/L |
| `keff_pbmc` (MRP4 leak, returns to plasma) | 3.4e10 1/h | Table S1 `kleak` (assumed for model); code `KL`; return term from Eq. S2a and MATLAB `dy(1)` |
| `gsh_int`, `gsh_ext` | 3100, 20 uM | Table S1 `GSHi`, `GSHe`; code `GSHI`, `GSHO` |
| Passive diffusion | `diffusion` | Eq. S1b, S2a, S2c |
| `ps_pbmc` | 0 L/h | Supplement text ("choosing PS_PBMC as 0"); Table S1 `PScell` |
| TFV -> TFV-MP (adenylate kinase 2) | `phos1` | Eq. S1f, S2c, S2d; code |
| `kcat_ak2`, `km_ak2`, `enz_ak2` | 2.4 1/s, 3 mM, 56 nM | Table S1 `kcat1`, `Km1`, `E1`; code |
| TFV-MP -> TFV-DP (NDPK-A) | `phos2` | Eq. S1g, S2d, S2e; code |
| `kcat_ndpk`, `km_ndpk`, `enz_ndpk` | 0.12 1/s, 0.29 mM, 287.7 nM | Table S1 `kcat2`, `Km2`, `E2`; code |
| `lkel_tfvdp` | log(0.0144375) 1/h | code `KO=0.0144375` (Table S1 `kout` = 0.0144, rounded) |
| Molecular weights (`model()`) | 287.2, 367.2, 447.18 g/mol | Table S1 `M_TFV`, `M_TFV-MP`, `M_TFV-DP`; code `M1`-`M3` |
| `etalcl`, `etalvc`, `etalvp` | 0.36, 0.79, 0.42 | NONMEM `$OMEGA` |
| `propSd`, `propSd_Cpbmc_tfvdp` | sqrt(0.183), sqrt(0.567) | NONMEM `$SIGMA` |
| `Cc` (ng/mL) | `1000 * central / vc` | MATLAB `CTFV`; NONMEM `C1` |
| `Cpbmc_tfvmp` (ng/mL of PBMC volume) | `1000 * pbmc_tfvmp / v_pbmc` | MATLAB `TFVMP` |
| `Cpbmc_tfvdp` ("fmol/10^6 cells") | `1e6 * pbmc_tfvdp / 447.18` | MATLAB `TFVDP`; NONMEM `C5` |

## Units

Amount states are carried in mg; the authors' code carried grams. Each rate law
converts its literature constants explicitly in `model()`, so the equations
are the authors' equations, not rescaled ones. One identity is worth checking
here because it is the easiest to get wrong: the uptake Km is tabulated in
micromolar, while the code carries it as a mass concentration.

```{r unit-identities}
mod <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Madrasi_2014_tenofovir_qsp"))
ini_df <- mod$iniDf
theta <- setNames(ini_df$est, ini_df$name)

# Code: KM = 0.000044229 g/L. 0.154 uM x 287.2 g/mol = 4.4229e-5 g/L.
km_g_per_l <- theta[["km_pbmc"]] * 1e-6 * 287.2
stopifnot(abs(km_g_per_l - 0.000044229) / 0.000044229 < 1e-4)

# Code: VC2 = VC1 * N = 2.8e-13 L x 4.5e9 = 1.26e-3 L.
v_pbmc <- theta[["n_pbmc"]] * theta[["v_blood"]] * 1000 *
  theta[["v_pbmc_cell"]] * 1e-12
stopifnot(abs(v_pbmc - 1.26e-3) < 1e-12)

# Table S1 PScell = 36.3 pL/h per cell; total over all cells (Eq. S1b):
ps_total <- 36.3e-12 * theta[["n_pbmc"]] * theta[["v_blood"]] * 1000
ps_total
```

# Deterministic single-dose simulations (Figures 2-4)

```{r single-dose}
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod, "omega")

scenarios <- list(
  "Diffusion + channel (Figure 2)" = c(km_pbmc = 770, keff_pbmc = 1.5e7,
                                       ps_pbmc = ps_total),
  "Channel only (Figure 3)" = c(km_pbmc = 770, keff_pbmc = 1.5e7, ps_pbmc = 0),
  "Saturable uptake (Figure 4)" = c(km_pbmc = 0.154, keff_pbmc = 3.4e10,
                                    ps_pbmc = 0)
)
doses <- c(75, 150, 300, 600)

make_events <- function(dose, dose_times, obs_times) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = 1L, time = dose_times, amt = dose, evid = 1L,
               cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_),
    data.frame(id = 1L, time = obs_times, amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L,
               cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

run_grid <- function(dose_times, obs_times) {
  out <- list()
  for (sc in names(scenarios)) {
    for (d in doses) {
      s <- rxode2::rxSolve(
        mod_typ, make_events(d, dose_times, obs_times),
        params = scenarios[[sc]], returnType = "data.frame",
        useLinCmt = FALSE
      )
      out[[length(out) + 1L]] <- s |>
        dplyr::select(time, Cc, Cpbmc_tfvmp, Cpbmc_tfvdp) |>
        dplyr::mutate(scenario = sc, dose = d)
    }
  }
  dplyr::bind_rows(out) |>
    dplyr::mutate(scenario = factor(scenario, levels = names(scenarios)),
                  dose = factor(paste(dose, "mg"), levels = paste(doses, "mg")))
}

sd_sim <- run_grid(0, seq(0, 240, by = 0.5))
```

```{r fig-single-dose, fig.height = 7.5}
# Replicates Figures 2, 3 and 4 of Madrasi 2014 (one row per figure).
sd_sim |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Cc, Cpbmc_tfvdp, Cpbmc_tfvmp), names_to = "output") |>
  dplyr::mutate(output = factor(output,
    levels = c("Cc", "Cpbmc_tfvdp", "Cpbmc_tfvmp"),
    labels = c("Plasma TFV (ng/mL)", "PBMC TFV-DP (fmol/1e6 cells)",
               "PBMC TFV-MP (ng/mL)"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value, colour = dose)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(scenario ~ output, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 240, 60)) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = NULL, colour = "TDF dose") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(strip.text.y = element_text(size = 7))
```

The figure reproduces the paper's three panels-of-three. The checks below
compare the peak of each curve with values the maintainers read off the
published figures (axis-limited, so about 3-5 percent reading precision), and
the 300 mg saturable peak with the number printed in Results.

```{r single-dose-checks}
peaks <- sd_sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(scenario, dose) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    plasma_cmax = max(Cc),
    tfvdp_cmax = max(Cpbmc_tfvdp),
    tfvdp_tmax = time[which.max(Cpbmc_tfvdp)],
    tfvmp_cmax = max(Cpbmc_tfvmp),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

published_peaks <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario,                        ~dose,    ~tfvdp_pub, ~tfvmp_pub,
  "Channel only (Figure 3)",        "75 mg",  3.0,        200,
  "Channel only (Figure 3)",        "150 mg", 6.0,        410,
  "Channel only (Figure 3)",        "300 mg", 12.0,       810,
  "Channel only (Figure 3)",        "600 mg", 23.7,       1620,
  "Saturable uptake (Figure 4)",    "75 mg",  4.8,        230,
  "Saturable uptake (Figure 4)",    "150 mg", 7.7,        320,
  "Saturable uptake (Figure 4)",    "300 mg", 11.35,      400,
  "Saturable uptake (Figure 4)",    "600 mg", 15.7,       460
)

peak_cmp <- peaks |>
  dplyr::mutate(scenario = as.character(scenario),
                dose = as.character(dose)) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(published_peaks, by = c("scenario", "dose")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    tfvdp_pct = 100 * (tfvdp_cmax - tfvdp_pub) / tfvdp_pub,
    tfvmp_pct = 100 * (tfvmp_cmax - tfvmp_pub) / tfvmp_pub
  )

peak_cmp |>
  dplyr::select(scenario, dose, tfvdp_cmax, tfvdp_pub, tfvdp_pct,
                tfvmp_cmax, tfvmp_pub, tfvmp_pct) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Scenario" = scenario, "TDF dose" = dose,
    "TFV-DP peak, model" = tfvdp_cmax, "TFV-DP peak, paper" = tfvdp_pub,
    "TFV-DP % diff" = tfvdp_pct,
    "TFV-MP peak, model (ng/mL)" = tfvmp_cmax,
    "TFV-MP peak, paper (ng/mL)" = tfvmp_pub,
    "TFV-MP % diff" = tfvmp_pct
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = paste(
    "Peak PBMC TFV-DP (fmol/1e6 cells) and TFV-MP after one TDF dose.",
    "Paper values are read from Figures 3 and 4, except the 300 mg",
    "saturable TFV-DP peak, which is printed in Results (11.35)."))

# The model is deterministic and has no random draw, so these bounds only
# have to absorb the figure-reading precision.
stopifnot(
  # Results: "The single-dose simulations of TDF dose at 300 mg reveal a
  # TFV-DP peak of 11.35 fmol/10^6 cells".
  abs(peaks$tfvdp_cmax[peaks$scenario == "Saturable uptake (Figure 4)" &
                         peaks$dose == "300 mg"] - 11.35) / 11.35 < 0.01,
  all(abs(peak_cmp$tfvdp_pct) < 10),
  all(abs(peak_cmp$tfvmp_pct) < 10),
  # Results "Impact of diffusion": "No difference was observed between the
  # two scenarios".
  max(abs(sd_sim$Cpbmc_tfvdp[sd_sim$scenario == "Diffusion + channel (Figure 2)"] -
            sd_sim$Cpbmc_tfvdp[sd_sim$scenario == "Channel only (Figure 3)"])) < 0.01
)
```

# Deterministic multiple-dose simulations (Figures S1-S3)

The authors simulated repeated dosing in MATLAB by restarting the ODE solver
once per dose (Supplement code): each restart takes its initial state from row
23 of the previous segment's `0:1:23` time grid, which is t = 22 h, not 24 h.
The first interval is therefore 23 h and every later one 22 h, although the
supplementary figures are drawn on a 24-hour axis. The packaged model is
simulated both ways below. Only the authors' 22-hour schedule reproduces the
channel-only plateau in Figure S2. The saturable plateau barely depends on the
interval, because its uptake runs near its maximum rate either way.

```{r multi-dose}
authors_times <- c(0, 23, 23 + 22 * (1:19))  # 20 doses, as in Figure S1-S3
md_authors <- run_grid(authors_times,
                       seq(0, max(authors_times) + 22, by = 0.5)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(schedule = "authors' MATLAB loop (22 h)")
md_daily <- run_grid(seq(0, 19 * 24, by = 24), seq(0, 480, by = 0.5)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(schedule = "true once daily (24 h)")

md_end <- dplyr::bind_rows(md_authors, md_daily) |>
  dplyr::group_by(schedule, scenario, dose) |>
  dplyr::summarise(tfvdp_end = dplyr::last(Cpbmc_tfvdp), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r fig-multi-dose}
# Replicates panel B of Figures S2 and S3 of Madrasi 2014 (authors' schedule).
md_authors |>
  dplyr::filter(scenario != "Diffusion + channel (Figure 2)") |>
  dplyr::mutate(scenario = sub("Figure 3", "Figure S2",
                               sub("Figure 4", "Figure S3", scenario))) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Cpbmc_tfvdp, colour = dose)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~scenario) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "PBMC TFV-DP (fmol/1e6 cells)", colour = "TDF dose") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r multi-dose-checks}
published_end <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario,                     ~dose,    ~tfvdp_end_pub,
  "Channel only (Figure 3)",     "75 mg",  17,
  "Channel only (Figure 3)",     "150 mg", 34,
  "Channel only (Figure 3)",     "300 mg", 68,
  "Channel only (Figure 3)",     "600 mg", 135,
  "Saturable uptake (Figure 4)", "75 mg",  20,
  "Saturable uptake (Figure 4)", "150 mg", 28,
  "Saturable uptake (Figure 4)", "300 mg", 35,
  "Saturable uptake (Figure 4)", "600 mg", 40
)

end_cmp <- md_end |>
  dplyr::mutate(scenario = as.character(scenario), dose = as.character(dose)) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(published_end, by = c("scenario", "dose")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct = 100 * (tfvdp_end - tfvdp_end_pub) / tfvdp_end_pub)

end_cmp |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = c(scenario, dose, tfvdp_end_pub),
                     names_from = schedule, values_from = c(tfvdp_end, pct)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Scenario" = scenario, "TDF dose" = dose,
    "Paper (Fig. S2/S3)" = tfvdp_end_pub,
    "Model, 22 h" = `tfvdp_end_authors' MATLAB loop (22 h)`,
    "% diff, 22 h" = `pct_authors' MATLAB loop (22 h)`,
    "Model, 24 h" = `tfvdp_end_true once daily (24 h)`,
    "% diff, 24 h" = `pct_true once daily (24 h)`
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = paste(
    "PBMC TFV-DP (fmol/1e6 cells) at the end of 20 doses. Paper values are",
    "read from panel B of Figures S2 and S3; the 300 mg saturable value is",
    "also printed in Results ('end TFV-DP amount of 35 fmol/10^6 cells')."))

authors_cmp <- end_cmp[end_cmp$schedule == "authors' MATLAB loop (22 h)", ]
daily_cmp <- end_cmp[end_cmp$schedule == "true once daily (24 h)", ]
stopifnot(
  all(abs(authors_cmp$pct) < 6),
  # The 24 h schedule misses the linear (channel-only) plateau by about 9
  # percent -- exactly the 24/22 dosing-rate ratio -- which is what
  # identifies the 22 h restart in the authors' code.
  all(abs(daily_cmp$pct[daily_cmp$scenario == "Channel only (Figure 3)"] + 9) < 3)
)
```

# Population simulation (Figure 5)

```{r population-sim}
n_sub <- 200L  # the paper simulated 100
pop_dose_times <- seq(0, 13 * 24, by = 24)
pop_obs_times <- c(seq(0, 12, by = 0.5), 13 * 24 + seq(0, 12, by = 0.5))
pop_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  expand.grid(id = seq_len(n_sub), time = pop_dose_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = 300, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_),
  expand.grid(id = seq_len(n_sub), time = pop_obs_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(123456)  # the seed in the authors' $SIM record
pop_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, pop_events, returnType = "data.frame",
                           useLinCmt = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::mutate(day = ifelse(time < 24, "Day 1", "Day 14"),
                tad = ifelse(time < 24, time, time - 13 * 24))

pop_q <- pop_sim |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Cc, Cpbmc_tfvdp), names_to = "output") |>
  dplyr::group_by(day, output, tad) |>
  dplyr::summarise(p05 = quantile(value, 0.05), p50 = median(value),
                   p95 = quantile(value, 0.95), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::mutate(output = factor(output, levels = c("Cc", "Cpbmc_tfvdp"),
    labels = c("Plasma TFV (ng/mL)", "PBMC TFV-DP (fmol/1e6 cells)")))
```

```{r fig-population, fig.height = 6}
# Replicates Figure 5 of Madrasi 2014: 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles of
# individual predictions (black: 5th / 95th, red: median). The MTN-001
# observations overlaid in the paper are not redistributable here.
ggplot(pop_q, aes(tad)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p05)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p95)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(output ~ day, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r population-checks}
pop_cmax14 <- pop_sim |>
  dplyr::filter(day == "Day 14") |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(tfvdp_cmax = max(Cpbmc_tfvdp), .groups = "drop")

pick_q <- function(o, d, t, col) {
  v <- pop_q[[col]][pop_q$output == o & pop_q$day == d & pop_q$tad == t]
  stopifnot(length(v) == 1L)
  v
}
plasma <- "Plasma TFV (ng/mL)"
tfvdp <- "PBMC TFV-DP (fmol/1e6 cells)"

pop_tab <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Quantity, ~Paper, ~Model,
  "Day 14 median TFV-DP Cmax (fmol/1e6 cells; Discussion)", 38.5,
    median(pop_cmax14$tfvdp_cmax),
  "Day 1 median plasma TFV at 2 h (ng/mL; Figure 5a)", 195,
    pick_q(plasma, "Day 1", 2, "p50"),
  "Day 1 median TFV-DP at 12 h (fmol/1e6 cells; Figure 5b)", 4.5,
    pick_q(tfvdp, "Day 1", 12, "p50"),
  "Day 14 median plasma TFV at 1 h (ng/mL; Figure 5c)", 320,
    pick_q(plasma, "Day 14", 1, "p50"),
  "Day 14 5th percentile TFV-DP (fmol/1e6 cells; Figure 5d)", 8,
    pick_q(tfvdp, "Day 14", 6, "p05"),
  "Day 14 95th percentile TFV-DP (fmol/1e6 cells; Figure 5d)", 238,
    pick_q(tfvdp, "Day 14", 6, "p95")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate("% diff" = 100 * (Model - Paper) / Paper)
knitr::kable(pop_tab, digits = 1, caption = paste(
  "Population simulation against the values printed in the Discussion and",
  "read from Figure 5."))

# Centre checks only: the paper's own percentiles come from 100 random
# subjects, and rxode2's random stream differs across builds and thread
# counts, so the extremes are not reproducible (see the 95th percentile row).
stopifnot(
  # TFV-DP spreads about 1 log unit between subjects, so a 200-subject median
  # moves about +/-10 percent with the draw, and the paper's 38.5 is itself a
  # 100-subject median (1000 subjects give 34). A unit or structural error
  # moves this by orders of magnitude.
  abs(median(pop_cmax14$tfvdp_cmax) - 38.5) / 38.5 < 0.40,
  abs(pick_q(plasma, "Day 1", 2, "p50") - 195) / 195 < 0.25,
  abs(pick_q(tfvdp, "Day 1", 12, "p50") - 4.5) / 4.5 < 0.35
)
```

The day-1 percentiles and the day-14 TFV-DP median and 5th percentile agree
with the paper. Two values do not:

* The 95th percentile of day-14 TFV-DP in Figure 5d is drawn at about 238,
  but the Discussion gives the simulated individual range as 4.715 to 139.5
  fmol/10^6 cells. With 100 subjects the 95th percentile cannot exceed the
  maximum, so the paper contradicts itself. This model's 95th percentile
  (about `r round(pick_q(tfvdp, "Day 14", 6, "p95"))`) is of the order of the
  printed maximum, not of the drawn line.
* The day-14 plasma median is about 10-15 percent below the Figure 5c line.
  On day 1 the medians match, and the typical-value accumulation is fixed by
  the Duwal 2012 PK, so the gap is consistent with sampling noise in a
  100-subject percentile plus figure-reading error.

# PKNCA: single-dose plasma TFV and PBMC TFV-DP

The paper reports a single-dose plasma tmax of 2 h ("as predicted before") and
the 300 mg TFV-DP peak quoted above. PKNCA is run on the saturable single-dose
profiles on the authors' 1-hour output grid (`tspan = 0:1:240`), with the dose
as the treatment group. Plasma `cl.obs` checks the PK chain end to end: almost
none of the absorbed tenofovir is lost to phosphorylation, so dose / AUC must
recover CL/F = 29.28 / 0.32 = 91.5 L/h.

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- sd_sim |>
  dplyr::filter(scenario == "Saturable uptake (Figure 4)",
                time == round(time)) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = 1L, treatment = as.character(dose),
                dose_mg = as.numeric(sub(" mg", "", treatment))) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, dose_mg, time, Cc, Cpbmc_tfvdp)

nca_conc <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  nca_conc,
  nca_conc |> dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, dose_mg) |>
    dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0, Cpbmc_tfvdp = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(treatment, time)

dose_df <- nca_conc |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, dose_mg) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = dose_mg)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)

res_tfv <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  dose_obj,
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                         aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
))
res_dp <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cpbmc_tfvdp ~ time | treatment + id),
  dose_obj,
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 240, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                         auclast = TRUE)
))

nca_tfv <- as.data.frame(res_tfv) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::mutate(clf = as.numeric(sub(" mg", "", treatment)) * 1000 / aucinf.obs) |>
  dplyr::arrange(as.numeric(sub(" mg", "", treatment)))
nca_dp <- as.data.frame(res_dp) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

dplyr::inner_join(nca_tfv, nca_dp, by = "treatment", suffix = c("_tfv", "_dp")) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, cmax_tfv, tmax_tfv, aucinf.obs, half.life, clf,
                cmax_dp, tmax_dp, auclast) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "TDF dose" = treatment, "Plasma Cmax (ng/mL)" = cmax_tfv,
    "Plasma Tmax (h)" = tmax_tfv, "Plasma AUC0-inf (ng*h/mL)" = aucinf.obs,
    "Plasma t1/2 (h)" = half.life, "CL/F (L/h)" = clf,
    "TFV-DP Cmax (fmol/1e6 cells)" = cmax_dp, "TFV-DP Tmax (h)" = tmax_dp,
    "TFV-DP AUC0-240" = auclast
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

stopifnot(
  # Dose / AUC recovers CL/F = 91.5 L/h. The 1-hour grid's trapezoids
  # under-read the absorption peak, which biases CL/F up by about 1 percent
  # (92.4 L/h here; a 0.05 h grid gives 91.5).
  all(abs(nca_tfv$clf - 29.28 / 0.32) / (29.28 / 0.32) < 0.02),
  # Plasma exposure is linear in dose; TFV-DP is not (saturable uptake).
  diff(range(nca_tfv$cmax / as.numeric(sub(" mg", "", nca_tfv$treatment)))) /
    mean(nca_tfv$cmax / as.numeric(sub(" mg", "", nca_tfv$treatment))) < 1e-3,
  nca_dp$cmax[nca_dp$treatment == "600 mg"] /
    nca_dp$cmax[nca_dp$treatment == "75 mg"] < 4
)
```

## Comparison against published values

```{r nca-compare}
simulated_wide <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("300 mg plasma TFV", "300 mg PBMC TFV-DP"),
  tmax = c(nca_tfv$tmax[nca_tfv$treatment == "300 mg"], NA_real_),
  cmax = c(NA_real_, nca_dp$cmax[nca_dp$treatment == "300 mg"])
)
published_wide <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("300 mg plasma TFV", "300 mg PBMC TFV-DP"),
  # Results: "The simulations for the single dose give a plasma TFV tmax of
  # 2 h"; "a TFV-DP peak of 11.35 fmol/10^6 cells".
  tmax = c(2, NA_real_),
  cmax = c(NA_real_, 11.35)
)
knitr::kable(nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = simulated_wide, reference = published_wide,
  by = "treatment", units = c(tmax = "h", cmax = "fmol/1e6 cells"),
  tolerance_pct = 20, label_first_column = "NCA parameter"
), caption = "Simulated vs. published. * differs from the paper by >20%.")
```

On a 1-hour grid the simulated plasma tmax falls at 1 or 2 h, because the
continuous-time peak lies between them (about 1.5 h). The paper's "2 h" is the
same coarse-grid reading.

# Sensitivity direction (Table 1)

Table 1 reports Latin-hypercube regression coefficients for the single-dose
300 mg TFV-DP Cmax and marks four as significant: kcat1 and E1 positive, Km1
and kleak negative. A local one-at-a-time +10 percent perturbation of the
packaged model gives the same signs.

```{r sensitivity}
base_ev <- make_events(300, 0, seq(0, 240, by = 0.5))
cmax_with <- function(p) {
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, base_ev, params = p,
                       returnType = "data.frame", useLinCmt = FALSE)
  max(s$Cpbmc_tfvdp)
}
base_cmax <- cmax_with(c(ps_pbmc = 0))
sens <- tibble::tibble(
  parameter = c("kcat_ak2", "enz_ak2", "km_ak2", "keff_pbmc"),
  paper_beta = c(1.4056, 1.3428, -0.4518, -1.1626)
) |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::mutate(local_elasticity = {
    p <- setNames(1.1 * theta[[parameter]], parameter)
    (cmax_with(p) / base_cmax - 1) / 0.1
  }) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()
sens |>
  dplyr::rename("Parameter" = parameter, "Paper beta (Table 1)" = paper_beta,
                "Local elasticity (+10%)" = local_elasticity) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
stopifnot(all(sign(sens$local_elasticity) == sign(sens$paper_beta)))
```

The magnitudes need not agree: the paper's coefficients come from 50 joint
random draws regressed together, not from local derivatives. Its non-significant
coefficients (for example a negative kcat2) are not interpretable as
directions.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **MRP4 leak returns tenofovir to plasma.** Supplement Eq. S2a and the MATLAB
  code add `+ kleak * Z3` to the plasma equation; the printed NONMEM `$DES`
  omits it. Without the return term the 3.4e10 1/h leak removes all plasma
  tenofovir within seconds, which contradicts every published figure. The
  model follows Eq. S2a and the MATLAB code.
* **All-cell PBMC volume in the Michaelis-Menten denominators.** The MATLAB
  listing divides the PBMC amounts by the volume of ONE cell (`Vcell`) in the
  efflux and phosphorylation terms; the NONMEM listing, and Eq. S1i (`V_cell x
  N x V_bl`), use the volume of all PBMCs. Only the all-cell volume reproduces
  Figures 2-4, so the model uses it. The MATLAB listing also refers to an
  undefined `Km3` in the TFV-DP equation, where `Km2` is meant.
* **Uptake Km and unionised fraction.** The code expresses the uptake Km as a
  mass concentration (0.154 uM x 287.2 g/mol) and omits the (1 - F) factor of
  Eq. S1h-S1i; F = 4.2e-5 changes nothing. The model follows the code.
* **TDF dosed as tenofovir.** As in the authors' code, the TDF dose in mg
  enters plasma tenofovir scaled only by Fbio = 0.32, with no TDF-to-tenofovir
  molecular-weight conversion (one 300 mg tablet carries 136 mg tenofovir).
* **TFV-DP readout.** `Cpbmc_tfvdp` is the authors' reported quantity:
  `A * 1e15 / (M3 * 1e6)` with the amount A in g (MATLAB `TFVDP`, NONMEM
  `C5`). It is the total TFV-DP amount in all PBMCs, in fmol, divided by
  10^6, not by the number of millions of cells (4500). It is therefore not a
  physical per-cell amount, and the assumed kleak and Km, which the authors
  chose to match clinical TFV-DP levels on this scale, are calibrated to it.
  Keep the readout if you change the parameters.
* **kout.** The code value 0.0144375 1/h is used; Table S1 rounds it to 0.0144.
* **Passive diffusion term.** Its form follows Eq. S2a (`fu * PS / Vc * (Z1 -
  Z3)`), with Table S1's per-cell PS (36.3 pL/h, which already includes the
  unionised fraction) summed over all PBMCs. The paper ran nonzero PS only in
  MATLAB with no listing, and it makes no visible difference (Figure 2 vs
  Figure 3), so the form cannot be checked further. It is zero in the final
  model.
* **Between-subject variability.** The NONMEM `$OMEGA` values (0.36, 0.79,
  0.42 on CL, Vc, Vp) are used as variances, as NONMEM reads them. The text
  attributes them to Baheti 2011, whose published variances differ (see
  `Baheti_2011_tenofovir`); the code is what was simulated.
* **Residual error.** The NONMEM `$ERROR` attaches the first proportional
  error to `CMT.EQ.1`, the absorption compartment, which is never observed; it
  is taken to belong to plasma tenofovir. The paper's percentiles are of
  individual predictions, so residual error does not enter any reproduced
  figure.
* **Multiple-dose schedule.** The supplementary figures come from a MATLAB
  restart loop whose effective dosing interval is 22 h (23 h for the first);
  see the multiple-dose section. The population simulation in NONMEM used true
  24-hour dosing.
* **Not reproduced.** The MTN-001 observations overlaid on Figure 5, and the
  Latin-hypercube sensitivity analysis itself (Figure S4, Table 1
  magnitudes), which depend on random draws the paper does not give.
